factsAccepted: ARR grew 50% YoY from $8M to $12M, an impressive headline. Over the same period, monthly churn rose from 2% to 4% -- a 100% increase in the churn rate. Net new account growth still appears healthy because acquisition is outpacing churn, but the churn trend is the opposite of what a 'product-market-fit victory' narrative implies.

Monthly churn of 4% implies roughly 39% annualized logo churn, and blended net revenue retention has slipped to ~96% (below the 100%+ that signals durable retention). The company has not produced cohort retention curves, so whether recent cohorts retain worse than older ones -- the key question for whether growth is healthy -- is unknown.

The category is dominated by Slack and Microsoft Teams, with limited differentiation and low switching costs. Rising churn in this context could reflect competitive displacement, but no win/loss analysis versus the incumbents has been produced, so the competitive contribution to churn is unmeasured.

No engagement-depth or activation metrics by cohort have been analyzed, and no churn-reason/exit-survey data exists. Whether churning accounts ever activated (onboarded to real value) or churned for reliability, usability, or unmet-value reasons is unknown -- precisely the evidence needed to tell a quality/retention problem apart from incidental churn or competitive loss.
